sections.body: Artificial intelligence in economics and investing now means machine learning models that forecast macroeconomic series, execute trades, screen private companies, score credit risk, build portfolios, parse financial language, ingest alternative data, automate back office workflows, trade crypto assets, and check fiduciary rules. The work is operational rather than theoretical, with banks and funds running these models daily on real order flow, loan books, and filings. Macroeconomic Econometrics uses gradient boosting and neural networks to nowcast GDP and inflation from high frequency releases. Quantitative Trading uses reinforcement learning and execution algorithms to place orders and manage inventory. Private Equity and Deal Sourcing uses language models to read company databases and flag acquisition targets, while Fixed Income and Credit Risk uses survival models and graph networks to estimate default probabilities. Portfolio Construction, Reading the Market's Language, Alternative Data, Agent Workflows in Finance, Crypto Markets and Decentralised Finance, and Governance and Fiduciary Risk extend the same pattern to asset allocation, text parsing, new data sources, workflow automation, on chain markets, and compliance monitoring.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The state of the field is uneven. Trade execution and text parsing are relatively mature, with models routinely beating simple benchmarks on latency and sentiment classification. Credit risk and macroeconomic forecasting remain hard because defaults and recessions are rare, data is nonstationary, and feedback loops change the distribution after models are deployed. Portfolio construction has solved parts of the optimisation problem but still struggles with unstable correlations and tail risk. Alternative data and agent workflows show real productivity gains in narrow tasks, yet they fail when asked to reason across regimes or explain causal chains. Crypto markets offer clean data and continuous trading, but their models are often overfit to short histories and wash trading. Governance and fiduciary risk is the least solved area, because existing rules were written for human decision makers and do not map cleanly onto model outputs.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Macroeconomic Econometrics and Quantitative Trading are the two entry points for prediction and execution, showing how models turn data into forecasts and orders. Private Equity and Deal Sourcing and Fixed Income and Credit Risk move from public markets to private assets and lending, where data is sparser and decisions are slower. Portfolio Construction and Reading the Market's Language sit in the middle, one turning signals into positions and the other turning text into signals. Alternative Data and Agent Workflows in Finance cover the inputs and the automation layer, from satellite imagery to multi step model chains. Crypto Markets and Decentralised Finance and Governance and Fiduciary Risk close the section with newer venues and the rules that bind all of the above. Across these pages, the site tracks 117 listed AI-related instruments with daily prices, which gives a concrete view of the public market side of the work.
